checkpoints.note: The recovered progressive Huffman scan headers satisfy the validation at this site, so the decoder does not raise `JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION` and instead enters the progression-status update loop on both scans. The witness headers are `scan0: n=3, comps={1,2,3}, Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1` and `scan1: n=1, comp={1}, Ss=1, Se=5, Ah=0, Al=2`.

First project-code read that creates vulnerability-relevant JPEG state: `get_sof()` pulls the component count from the recovered SOF header. For the staged witness this byte is `3`, which sizes the later `coef_bits` / `prev_coef_bits` tables and the all-component smoothing loops.

checkpoints.code: for (coefi = MIN(cinfo->Ss, 1); coefi <= MAX(cinfo->Se, 9); coefi++) { if (cinfo->input_scan_number > 1) prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi] = coef_bit_ptr[coefi]; }
checkpoints.note: On the first progressive Huffman scan, this loop has no `else` initialization for `prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi]` when `input_scan_number == 1`. The step therefore leaves each component's `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` undefined even though later block-smoothing code assumes those previous-scan entries are initialized. The fix patch adds `else prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi] = 0;` at this exact site; the recovered witness JPEG uses `SOF2`/`FFC4`, so the `jdphuff.c` side of the patch is the executed root cause.
